automotive-ev-battery.title: Heart Aerospace completes maiden flight of electric aircraft demonstrator X1
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Heart Aerospace has successfully completed the first flight of its battery-electric X1 demonstrator, marking a significant achievement as the largest electric aircraft ever flown. The demonstration aircraft will serve as the technical foundation for the company's ES-30 hybrid-electric regional aircraft development.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Nio launches first fifth-generation battery swap stations
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Nio has opened its first fifth-generation battery swap stations in China, expanding network compatibility to include Firefly models for the first time. The company has simultaneously reached a significant operational milestone of 4,000 battery swap stations across its domestic market.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Leapmotor A05 to challenge Geely E2
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Stellantis-backed Leapmotor has unveiled the A05, a 4.20-metre battery-electric compact car featuring a 70 kW front-wheel-drive system and 39.8 kWh LFP battery in its base version. The company plans to expand the model's availability beyond China to the European market.

automotive-ev-battery.title: TU Graz develops guidelines for repairable EV batteries
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Researchers at TU Graz have established design guidelines to enhance the safety, repairability, and recyclability of electric vehicle traction batteries. The analysis demonstrates that repair-oriented battery designs can deliver positive economic and environmental returns if as little as 8% of battery cells are recovered for reuse.

automotive-ev-battery.title: India extends electric two-wheeler incentives
automotive-ev-battery.summary: India's Ministry of Heavy Industries has extended the deadline for electric two-wheeler subsidies under the PM E-DRIVE Scheme to March 31, 2028, while increasing the scheme's total funding to 119 billion rupees. Nearly all additional funding has been allocated specifically to support electric two-wheeler adoption.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Neptune Energy advances Altmark lithium project
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Neptune Energy is progressing toward lithium production at Germany's Altmark region, with production targeted to commence in 2030. The company and Fraunhofer IEG are currently testing various adsorbent materials in a second pilot phase to optimize industrial-scale lithium extraction.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Aira EV Drives 68% of Wuling Orders at GIIAS 2026
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Wuling Motors secured 3,290 vehicle purchase orders at the 2026 Gaikindo Indonesia International Auto Show, with its Aira EV micro car accounting for 2,238 orders representing 68% of total sales. The strong performance demonstrates significant market demand for affordable compact electric vehicles in Southeast Asia.

automotive-ev-battery.title: As EV sales, oil costs and wildfires spike, UK gov't considers.. fewer EVs?
automotive-ev-battery.summary: The UK government is considering relaxing its stringent electric vehicle regulations despite rising EV sales already meeting government targets, elevated oil prices, and record-breaking temperatures and wildfire damage. The consultation launch comes amid ongoing climate concerns linked to fossil fuel vehicle emissions.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Ireland launches EV Flex smart charging trial
automotive-ev-battery.summary: ESB Networks and Ohme are launching a six-month smart charging trial in Ireland allowing EV drivers to earn up to €78 by providing grid flexibility through home charging timing. The initiative aims to optimize charging patterns while providing financial incentives to participating drivers.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Chery Buys Nissan Factory in Africa
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Chinese EV manufacturer Chery has acquired a Nissan factory in Africa as part of broader Chinese industry efforts to expand into international markets. This expansion reflects the maturation of China's domestic EV market, where electric vehicles accounted for approximately 43% of sales in June.

world-news.title: Trump vows to make Hormuz US territory 'pretty soon'
world-news.summary: US President Trump has stated he will declare the Strait of Hormuz a US territory once Iran is defeated, marking a significant escalation in ongoing US-Iran tensions. Control over the strategically critical strait has become a central issue in ceasefire negotiations between the two nations.

world-news.title: Lebanon's PM urges timetable for Israeli withdrawal as Hezbollah slams deal
world-news.summary: Lebanon's Prime Minister has called for a defined timeline for Israeli military withdrawal, while Hezbollah has criticized the government's negotiating approach as exposing the Lebanese army to Israeli pressure and risks. The disagreement reflects deepening divisions over ceasefire terms in the ongoing Israel-Lebanon conflict.

world-news.title: Afghan women tell the BBC their lives are unrecognisable after five years of Taliban rule
world-news.summary: Afghan women have documented severe restrictions on their rights and freedoms under Taliban governance, including public floggings, job losses, and healthcare barriers that endanger lives. The accounts illustrate the systemic rollback of women's rights since the Taliban's return to power in 2021.

world-news.title: Houthi attack on port kills four eroding truce with Yemen's government
world-news.summary: Six Houthi ballistic missiles struck Yemen's government-held al-Makha port, killing at least four people in an attack that threatens ongoing ceasefire efforts. The strike represents escalating hostilities between Iran-backed Houthis and Yemen's internationally recognized government.

world-news.title: Wildfires rage across Europe as heatwaves drive record temperatures
world-news.summary: Record-breaking heatwaves are fueling widespread wildfires across Europe, with approximately 500,000 hectares burned and thousands of residents forced to evacuate their homes. The crisis underscores the accelerating impacts of climate change on the continent.

world-news.title: Activists try to deliver aid to Palestinians in homes besieged by Israeli settlers
world-news.summary: Two Palestinian families have been trapped in their homes in the occupied West Bank for several days as activists attempt to deliver humanitarian aid. The incident reflects ongoing tensions between Palestinian residents and Israeli settlers in disputed territories.

world-news.title: France's top court blocks social media ban for under-15s
world-news.summary: France's Constitutional Council has rejected President Macron's proposed ban on social media for minors under 15, citing freedom of expression concerns. Macron has indicated his intention to draft revised legislation addressing the issue.

world-news.title: US aircraft carrier on way to relieve USS Lincoln after issues reported on board
world-news.summary: A replacement aircraft carrier has been dispatched to relieve the USS Lincoln amid widespread reports of deteriorating conditions, including food shortages, broken plumbing, and sailor morale crises. The incident has prompted congressional calls for an investigation into military readiness and personnel welfare.

world-news.title: Instagram accounts fuelling Ceuta crisis with paid advice for help to cross
world-news.summary: A network of Instagram profiles has been identified glamorizing and profiting from migrant crossings at the Morocco-Ceuta border, offering paid guidance for illegal border transit. The discovery highlights how social media facilitates irregular migration flows in the strategically sensitive Mediterranean region.

world-news.title: Israeli soldiers accused of supporting 'terrorist' settlers in Qusra
world-news.summary: Israeli military personnel have been accused of collaborating with settler militias designated as terrorist organizations in the West Bank community of Qusra. The allegations raise concerns about institutional complicity in extrajudicial violence against Palestinians.

science-space.title: NASA's COFFIES Uses AI to Predict Storm-Causing Active Regions on Sun
science-space.summary: NASA's COFFIES team has developed an artificial intelligence system to predict space weather conditions driven by solar activity, a capability increasingly vital as humanity prepares for lunar exploration and long-duration missions. The advancement in forecasting storm-causing regions on the Sun addresses a critical need for space weather prediction in support of future space operations.

science-space.title: Water can survive surprisingly close to the Milky Way's supermassive black hole, James Webb Space Telescope finds
science-space.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope has made a significant discovery that water and cosmic dust can survive in the extreme environment near Sagittarius A*, the supermassive black hole at the center of our galaxy. This finding challenges previous assumptions about the habitability of regions near black holes and expands understanding of molecular survival in extreme cosmic conditions.

science-space.title: US Space Force gives Rocket Lab $397 million to build threat-tracking 'Flatellites'
science-space.summary: The U.S. Space Force has awarded Rocket Lab a $397 million contract to manufacture a fleet of advanced satellites designed to detect and track airborne threats from space-based platforms. This investment represents a significant expansion of space-based defense capabilities and demonstrates growing military reliance on commercial space technology.

science-space.title: Is empty space really empty? This magnetic star may finally solve a 90-year-old mystery
science-space.summary: Astronomers are using observations of a magnetic star to test fundamental laws of physics and investigate whether empty space truly contains unknown properties or particles. This research demonstrates how astronomical observations can serve as natural laboratories to validate or challenge established scientific principles.

science-space.title: Will the new moon race turn Earth's nearest neighbor into a dumping ground?
science-space.summary: Scientific experts are calling for regulatory frameworks to prevent space companies from leaving abandoned rocket debris on the lunar surface as lunar exploration activity accelerates. The discussion highlights growing concerns about space debris and environmental protection as multiple nations and private companies pursue lunar missions.

science-space.title: NASA Competition Invites Students to Help Imagine a Future Enabled by Lunar Technologies
science-space.summary: NASA has announced the 2027 RASC-AL student competition, inviting U.S. collegiate teams to develop innovative concepts for lunar operations and technologies that could shape the future of Moon exploration. The challenge seeks bold, original ideas from student researchers to advance aerospace systems relevant to sustained lunar presence.

science-space.title: NASA Announces MAX POWER: America's Newest Aerospace Expo, Airshow
science-space.summary: NASA announced MAX POWER, a public aerospace exposition scheduled for November 7-8 at Kennedy Space Center in Florida, showcasing next-generation aircraft, spacecraft, and autonomous vehicles. The family-friendly event coincides with America's 250th anniversary and will highlight cutting-edge innovations defining the future of air and space technology.

science-space.title: Volunteer Develops Machine-Learning Tool to Identify Rare Clouds
science-space.summary: Scientists partnering with NASA have developed a machine-learning tool to identify rare cloud formations that are increasingly appearing lower in the atmosphere and with greater frequency than historical records indicate. The Space Cloud Watch project enlists public participation by requesting cloud images from observers worldwide to help understand factors influencing these atmospheric changes.

science-space.title: ISS photobombs the sun during solar eclipse | Space photo of the day for Aug. 14, 2026
science-space.summary: The International Space Station created a dramatic silhouette across the Sun's face during the total solar eclipse visible from Spain on August 12, 2026, producing a remarkable astronomical photograph. The rare alignment of the ISS transit during eclipse totality captured a unique convergence of orbital mechanics and celestial events.

science-space.title: Can Venus cast a shadow? Here's how to see it for yourself
science-space.summary: As Venus approaches its greatest brightness in the evening sky, astronomers are highlighting an unusual phenomenon: whether the planet can cast a visible shadow on Earth's surface. The article offers observers guidance on testing this astronomical claim through direct observation.

finance-markets.title: Jane Street suffers $15bn hit after meltdown at Situational Awareness
finance-markets.summary: Secretive Wall Street trading firm Jane Street incurred a $15 billion loss following a market disruption linked to the Situational Awareness platform during July's artificial intelligence sector downturn. The incident highlights the systemic risks posed by concentrated positions in algorithmic trading strategies.

finance-markets.title: Bally's Warns of Going Concern Doubt as It Seeks Fresh Liquidity
finance-markets.summary: Bally's Corp. has issued a going concern warning to investors, indicating substantial doubt about its ability to continue operations and signaling potential covenant violations with its lenders. The company is actively pursuing additional liquidity sources to address its financial distress.

finance-markets.title: Investors pile back into US stocks as bullishness returns to Wall Street
finance-markets.summary: U.S. equity markets have rebounded sharply as investors regain confidence, driven by stellar corporate earnings results and declining inflation data that offset July's technology sector volatility. The rally reflects renewed optimism among market participants regarding economic resilience and corporate profitability.

finance-markets.title: Nvidia discloses $21bn stake in SpaceX
finance-markets.summary: Nvidia has disclosed a substantial $21 billion equity stake in SpaceX, following Elon Musk's announcement of an exclusive partnership to supply computing infrastructure for SpaceX's data centers. The investment signals deepening integration between two of the world's most influential technology companies.

finance-markets.title: Americans sour on Trump's economy as affordability strains intensify
finance-markets.summary: Consumer sentiment and retail sales have declined as Americans face mounting affordability pressures exacerbated by elevated oil prices and regional geopolitical tensions. The economic data indicates deteriorating household purchasing power and weakening demand for discretionary goods.

finance-markets.title: Wall Street Week | Rerouting Global Trade, Private Equity Tested, Realizing Cuba's Potential
finance-markets.summary: Markets face persistent inflation challenges as the Federal Reserve's 2% target remains elusive, while private equity fund managers confront headwinds from rising borrowing costs and slowing exit opportunities. Structural developments including Mexico's new trade corridor and Cuba's market reforms present alternative investment themes for portfolio strategists.

finance-markets.title: Jane Street has paid up large to avoid its numbers leaking out
finance-markets.summary: Jane Street has accepted elevated financing costs to maintain strict confidentiality over its financial performance and trading positions. The preference for privacy over cheaper capital alternatives reflects the firm's strategic emphasis on information asymmetry in competitive trading markets.

finance-markets.title: Former Boston Fed Pres.: Investment spend a catalyst
finance-markets.summary: Former Boston Federal Reserve President Eric Rosengren attributes recent retail sales weakness to elevated oil prices pressuring consumer budgets while capital investment—driven by artificial intelligence and technology sector expansion—sustains overall economic growth. The divergence suggests an uneven economic recovery favoring corporate capital allocation over household consumption.

finance-markets.title: Unhappy voters are suffering from 'Baumol's disease'
finance-markets.summary: An economic analysis drawing on classical music sector dynamics explains voter dissatisfaction as a manifestation of Baumol's disease, wherein labor-intensive public services experience persistent cost inflation relative to productivity gains. The structural phenomenon accounts for widespread perception that tax burdens are rising despite deteriorating public service quality.

finance-markets.title: Antitrust Lawyer on NFL Streaming Cost Concerns
finance-markets.summary: Legal experts are examining potential antitrust implications as multiple streaming platforms fragmenting National Football League broadcast rights have driven up consumer costs significantly. The discussion highlights regulatory scrutiny of platform bundling strategies and pricing practices in the sports media industry.

tech-ai.title: Self-driving trucks are officially testing on California highways
tech-ai.summary: Aurora Innovation and Kodiak AI have received permits from California's Department of Motor Vehicles to test autonomous trucks on public highways, marking a significant milestone in the commercialization of self-driving technology. The approval enables real-world validation of autonomous vehicle capabilities in commercial trucking operations.

tech-ai.title: What we know about the alleged Iranian hacks on US water utilities
tech-ai.summary: Multiple water treatment facilities across the United States have been targeted in recent cyberattacks allegedly attributed to the Iranian government. The incident highlights critical vulnerabilities in infrastructure security and raises concerns about potential threats to essential services.

tech-ai.title: Apple proposes to take a 15% cut of purchases made outside the App Store
tech-ai.summary: Apple has petitioned a federal judge to permit commissions of up to 15 percent on transactions completed through external links within iOS applications, continuing its legal efforts to monetize App Store alternatives. The proposal represents a potential compromise in Apple's ongoing regulatory battles over app distribution policies.

tech-ai.title: Talks to sell PayPal to Stripe and Advent are heating up
tech-ai.summary: PayPal remains in active negotiations regarding a potential acquisition by fintech company Stripe and private equity firm Advent Capital as the payments giant pursues strategic alternatives under new leadership. The discussions underscore ongoing consolidation pressures within the fintech sector.

tech-ai.title: Does Mark Zuckerberg really believe AI is 'for everyone'?
tech-ai.summary: Meta released Glimmer, an open-weight AI model available for public download and deployment on personal hardware, contrasting with its proprietary Muse Spark offering and aligning with Zuckerberg's stated philosophy of democratizing artificial intelligence. The release raises questions about the authenticity of open-source commitments versus restricted commercial offerings.

tech-ai.title: Thrive's Joshua Kushner chides Silicon Valley VCs over AI euphoria
tech-ai.summary: Investment firm Thrive Capital's co-founder Joshua Kushner cautioned venture capitalists against letting artificial intelligence enthusiasm compromise investment discipline in his first-ever investment letter. Kushner acknowledged AI's substantial opportunity while urging the investor community to maintain rigorous evaluation standards.

tech-ai.title: The MSI Claw EX is the most important PC handheld since Steam Deck — I still wouldn't buy one
tech-ai.summary: The MSI Claw 8 EX AI Plus, equipped with next-generation Intel processors and improved design, represents the most capable portable gaming PC with superior battery life and reliable sleep functionality. Despite its technical achievements, reviewers express reservations about recommending the device for general purchase.

tech-ai.title: Google will now allow users to remove visible watermark from its AI generations
tech-ai.summary: Google has updated its AI generation tools to permit users to disable visible watermarks on AI-generated images, videos, and music while maintaining invisible SynthID authentication markers. The change offers greater creative flexibility while preserving technical mechanisms for AI-generated content identification.

tech-ai.title: Kog is going deeper to squeeze more inference out of GPUs
tech-ai.summary: French startup Kog challenges prevailing assumptions about GPU unsuitability for agentic artificial intelligence workflows, suggesting that graphics processors may be more capable for these applications than commonly believed. The company's research could influence optimization strategies for AI inference performance.

tech-ai.title: Google's best new camera feature is only for the Pixel 11 series
tech-ai.summary: Google introduced Camera Looks for the Pixel 11 lineup, a new computational photography feature that processes sensor-level image data to produce non-smartphone aesthetic results, including vintage digital camera styles. The advanced feature will initially remain exclusive to the latest Pixel generation.

cybersecurity.title: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 400 Security Holes
cybersecurity.summary: Microsoft released updates addressing at least 398 security vulnerabilities across Windows operating systems and supported software. The patch includes one actively exploited vulnerability and two others previously disclosed publicly, representing a critical monthly maintenance cycle for the world's most widely deployed OS.

cybersecurity.title: Max severity SAP Commerce Cloud flaw now targeted in attacks
cybersecurity.summary: A maximum-severity remote code execution vulnerability in SAP Commerce Cloud is already being actively exploited just three days after patches were released. The rapid weaponization of this critical flaw poses immediate risk to organizations running the e-commerce platform.

cybersecurity.title: 737 Chrome VPN Extensions Caught Routing Traffic Through Proxies
cybersecurity.summary: Security researchers identified 737 malicious VPN and proxy extensions on the Chrome Web Store targeting Russian-speaking users, with a total of 75,486 installations across at least 40 developer accounts. The extensions intercept browser traffic and route it through attacker-controlled proxy infrastructure, with 274 found to impersonate legitimate VPN services.

cybersecurity.title: Shell investigates 'potential incident' after Clop data theft claims
cybersecurity.summary: Oil giant Shell has launched an investigation following claims by the Clop ransomware gang that they stole 89GB of data from the company. The incident underscores ongoing threats to critical infrastructure sectors from sophisticated ransomware operations.

cybersecurity.title: Read This Before You Buy That TV Streaming Stick
cybersecurity.summary: Analysis reveals that generic TV streaming devices exploit users' internet connections for ad fraud, spoofing themselves as mobile devices to click ads on AI-generated websites as part of schemes defrauding merchants and advertising networks. The findings add to longstanding security warnings about devices promising unlimited streaming for one-time fees.

cybersecurity.title: Hackers arrested over €30M bank fraud exploiting service provider flaw
cybersecurity.summary: Four cybercriminals were arrested in Brazil and three charged in Europe for exploiting a vulnerability at a service provider to fraudulently withdraw funds from Commerzbank customer accounts totaling approximately €30 million. The case demonstrates the significant financial impact of supply-chain security failures in banking.

cybersecurity.title: Hackers exploit macOS Screen Sharing flaw to deploy Monero miner
cybersecurity.summary: The Netherlands' National Cyber Security Centre warned that threat actors are actively exploiting a macOS authentication bypass vulnerability following the release of public exploit code. The flaw is being leveraged to deploy cryptocurrency miners on compromised systems.

cybersecurity.title: Scattered Spider Hackers Plead Guilty on Day 1 of Trial
cybersecurity.summary: Two members of the prolific Scattered Spider cybercrime group pleaded guilty in the United Kingdom to charges related to an August 2024 cyberattack that disrupted Transport for London's operations. The guilty pleas on the trial's first day mark a significant enforcement success against one of the year's most active threat actors.

cybersecurity.title: Scottish Govt Suffers Potentially Widening Data Breach at Prosecutor's Office
cybersecurity.summary: A Scottish government agency, the Prosecutor's Office, reported a data breach potentially involving a third-party service provider that may have affected additional government agencies. The incident raises concerns about broader exposure across government digital infrastructure.

cybersecurity.title: 'Jewelbug' APT Balances State Espionage & Cryptocurrency Theft
cybersecurity.summary: Researchers identified a hackers-for-hire group conducting both state-sponsored cyber espionage and financially motivated cryptocurrency theft operations from the same command-and-control panel. The discovery illustrates the blurred line between nation-state and criminal cyber operations in modern threat landscapes.

startups-vc.title: Databricks Just Crossed $7B ARR Growing 80% (!): A 30-Point Acceleration, a $190B Valuation, and the Margin Bill for Agents
startups-vc.summary: Databricks announced it crossed $7 billion in annual recurring revenue run-rate in Q2 with over 80% year-over-year growth, closing a $5 billion strategic funding round at a $190 billion valuation led by Coatue. The achievement represents a significant acceleration in growth and signals major investor confidence in the AI infrastructure market.

startups-vc.title: The Week's 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: Data, Neolab, AI Infrastructure, Defense And AI Coding Lead
startups-vc.summary: Major funding rounds this week were dominated by data infrastructure, AI, defense, and coding platforms, with Databricks leading at $5 billion in fresh capital. The week reflects strong investor appetite for AI infrastructure and enterprise software solutions.

startups-vc.title: 40 Companies Joined The Unicorn Board In July, The Highest Count In 4 Years
startups-vc.summary: Forty companies achieved unicorn status in July 2026, marking the highest monthly count in four years, with leadership from financial services, robotics, AI orchestration, and semiconductor sectors. The U.S. accounted for nearly half of the newly minted unicorns, signaling robust startup ecosystem growth.

startups-vc.title: Klaviyo's CEO on Building at $1.5B With Agents: "Dark Factory," Composer, and Why Every Single Employee Had to Hit L3 by June
startups-vc.summary: Klaviyo co-founder and co-CEO Andrew Bialecki discussed how the 2,300-person public company is building AI products by fundamentally redesigning workflows and organizational structures around AI capabilities. The insights highlight practical approaches to integrating AI into mature B2B software operations at scale.

startups-vc.title: AI-Native, Not AI-Sprinkle: Why AI Is A Business Change, Not A Technology Change
startups-vc.summary: According to Strattam Capital co-founder Bob Morse, companies achieve transformational productivity gains from AI by redesigning teams, roles, and workflows around AI capabilities rather than simply adding AI tools to existing processes. The analysis emphasizes that meaningful AI value creation requires CEO and board-backed organizational change.

startups-vc.title: The VC Firm That Helped Build Latin America's Startup Scene Is Crossing Into Silicon Valley
startups-vc.summary: Monashees, one of Latin America's oldest and most influential venture firms, opened a San Francisco office to establish a permanent Silicon Valley presence, reflecting the next phase of the region's startup ecosystem evolution. The expansion signals how established regional VCs are positioning themselves for the AI-driven startup landscape.

startups-vc.title: Meta's 'Open' AI, and a $250M Deal Gone Very Wrong
startups-vc.summary: Meta released Glimmer, an open-weight AI model for public download and on-premises deployment, contrasting with its proprietary Muse Spark model, accompanied by Mark Zuckerberg's advocacy for democratized AI access. The announcement reflects ongoing industry tensions between open and closed AI development approaches.

startups-vc.title: Kog is going deeper to squeeze more inference out of GPUs
startups-vc.summary: French startup Kog challenges the assumption that GPUs are poorly suited for agentic AI workflows, suggesting optimization opportunities in current hardware utilization. The company's work addresses a critical infrastructure bottleneck in deploying large-scale AI agents.

startups-vc.title: Harshita Arora Joins YC as General Partner
startups-vc.summary: Y Combinator announced that Harshita Arora has joined as General Partner, bringing deep fintech and infrastructure experience along with a founder's perspective from building companies since her teenage years. The appointment strengthens YC's investment team during a critical period of AI infrastructure growth.

startups-vc.title: 5 Interesting Learnings from Palo Alto Networks at $11.4 Billion in Revenue: 60% ARR Growth, 120% NRR, and a $25B Acquisition That Doubled the Stock
startups-vc.summary: Palo Alto Networks reached $11.4 billion in revenue with 60% ARR growth and 120% net revenue retention through aggressive acquisition strategy totaling approximately $29 billion in twelve months. The case study demonstrates how mature enterprise software companies are scaling through M&A while maintaining strong operational metrics.

health-biotech.title: FDA approves Bristol multiple myeloma treatment, marking debut of novel drug class
health-biotech.summary: The FDA has approved Bristol Myers Squibb's Zenbexus for advanced multiple myeloma, marking the first approval of a new class of protein-degrading CELMoD medicines. This approval represents a significant therapeutic advancement for blood cancer treatment and a potential growth driver for the company's oncology portfolio.

health-biotech.title: Epic's alleged anticompetitive practices under scrutiny from federal, state investigators
health-biotech.summary: Epic Systems, a major healthcare IT vendor, is facing a broad federal and state inquiry into its business practices, according to individuals contacted by FTC investigators. The investigation marks a significant regulatory action against a company with substantial influence over healthcare data systems and interoperability.

health-biotech.title: Biogen's monoclonal antibody felzartamab wins first global approval in China
health-biotech.summary: Biogen's monoclonal antibody felzartamab has received approval in China for second-line multiple myeloma treatment in combination with lenalidomide and dexamethasone. This represents the first global regulatory approval for the drug and expands Biogen's presence in the Chinese oncology market.

health-biotech.title: Cytokinetics brings patent suit against Bristol Myers, escalating rivalry
health-biotech.summary: Cytokinetics has filed a patent lawsuit against Bristol Myers Squibb, seeking to invalidate a recently granted patent and intensifying the companies' competitive dispute. The legal action reflects growing tension between the two pharmaceutical rivals in the cardiovascular and muscle disease markets.

health-biotech.title: ICER says AstraZeneca's new blood pressure med isn't cost-effective
health-biotech.summary: The Institute for Clinical and Economic Review has determined that AstraZeneca's new blood pressure medication Baxfendy does not provide sufficient clinical benefit to justify its $10,950 annual price tag. The cost-effectiveness assessment may significantly impact the drug's market adoption and reimbursement landscape.

health-biotech.title: Capricor, seeking lifeline for Duchenne therapy, says it will ask FDA to review additional data
health-biotech.summary: Following a negative FDA advisory committee vote, Capricor Therapeutics announced plans to submit additional data and analyses for its Duchenne muscular dystrophy therapy in hopes of securing approval for a narrower patient indication. The resubmission strategy represents a potential pathway for the experimental cell therapy to reach patients despite initial regulatory setbacks.

health-biotech.title: Abcuro gets $66M for Phase 3 in muscle-weakening condition
health-biotech.summary: Abcuro Therapeutics has raised $66 million in funding to advance Phase 3 studies for its investigational treatment of a muscle-weakening condition, following mixed results in an earlier trial that showed promise in a subset of patients with less severe disease. The financing enables the company to pursue a potentially narrower indication with higher likelihood of clinical success.

health-biotech.title: PBMs agree to display TrumpRx drug prices
health-biotech.summary: Pharmacy benefit managers have agreed to display drug prices through a TrumpRx initiative, while Bristol's Zenbexus received accelerated FDA approval and Novartis secured a UK patent victory for Entresto. These developments reflect ongoing industry shifts in drug pricing transparency and intellectual property protection.

health-biotech.title: Drug-testing lab that has sparked controversy sues group that develops drug standards over criticism
health-biotech.summary: A controversial drug testing laboratory has filed a lawsuit against the U.S. Pharmacopeia, accusing the standards-setting organization of making false and misleading statements about its testing methods. The litigation highlights ongoing disputes over impurity detection in widely used medications and laboratory quality standards.

health-biotech.title: How will legal challenges fare against CMS rule on gender-affirming care?
health-biotech.summary: Legal experts assess the prospects for challenging a newly finalized CMS rule regarding gender-affirming care coverage, with analysis suggesting the rule may present different vulnerabilities than previous Trump administration healthcare policy actions. The regulatory decision has significant implications for healthcare access and coverage policy.

crypto-web3.title: Trump-backed World Liberty wins conditional bank charter from federal regulator
crypto-web3.summary: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency granted preliminary conditional approval to World Liberty Trust Co., marking a significant regulatory milestone for the Trump family's crypto financial venture. This approval represents a major step toward establishing a federally-regulated banking entity within the cryptocurrency space.

crypto-web3.title: Trump expected to attend White House meeting with crypto CEOs, sources say
crypto-web3.summary: President Donald Trump is anticipated to participate in a high-level White House gathering next week with leading cryptocurrency, prediction market, and artificial intelligence executives. The meeting signals potential direct engagement between the administration and key industry stakeholders on regulatory and policy matters.

crypto-web3.title: Cboe seeks SEC nod for first US 3x bitcoin and ether ETFs
crypto-web3.summary: Cboe Global Markets has filed for regulatory approval to launch the first 3x leveraged bitcoin and ether exchange-traded funds in the United States, following the European debut of similar products by LeverageShares. The filing represents an expansion of leverage-based cryptocurrency investment vehicles available to U.S. investors.

crypto-web3.title: Israel's largest bank to offer crypto trading with Galaxy
crypto-web3.summary: Bank Leumi will enable customers to trade bitcoin, ether, and solana through its investment application beginning in early 2027, partnering with Galaxy Digital. The expansion marks continued institutional adoption of cryptocurrency services within traditional banking infrastructure.

crypto-web3.title: Tokenization stocks slip as SEC delay puts 'speed bump' in crypto's Wall Street push
crypto-web3.summary: Shares of tokenization and blockchain companies including Bullish, Coinbase, and Circle declined following an SEC regulatory setback that delayed crypto market infrastructure expansion. The market reaction reflects investor concern about the timeline for institutional cryptocurrency adoption initiatives.

crypto-web3.title: Binance to block transactions with HTX, 10 other exchanges under EU Russia sanctions
crypto-web3.summary: Binance announced it will cease processing transactions from 16 exchanges, including HTX and other platforms, in compliance with European Union Russia sanctions requirements. The compliance measure affects cross-exchange settlement activities and reflects broader regulatory pressure on major cryptocurrency platforms.

crypto-web3.title: Norway sovereign wealth fund sees indirect bitcoin exposure hit all-time high, with Strategy accounting for 86%
crypto-web3.summary: Norges Bank Investment Management's indirect bitcoin exposure reached an all-time high, with the bitcoin treasury company Strategy representing 86% of the position, alongside a new $88 million investment in Ethereum treasury firm Bitmine. The holdings underscore growing acceptance of cryptocurrency assets within major institutional portfolios.

crypto-web3.title: 'Honestly, I don't care': Tether CEO dismisses critics following first KPMG audit
crypto-web3.summary: Tether's chief executive dismissed ongoing criticism of the stablecoin issuer following completion of its first KPMG audit, stating the company does not publicly share audited statements due to its private status. The response reflects tension between transparency demands from regulators and critics versus Tether's operational structure.

crypto-web3.title: RedotPay said to put $1 billion U.S. IPO plan on hold: Bloomberg
crypto-web3.summary: Stablecoin payments company RedotPay has postponed its planned $1 billion initial public offering in the United States, according to reporting by Bloomberg. A company representative declined to comment on the IPO delay or provide additional context for the decision.

crypto-web3.title: Mizuho cuts BitGo price target to $11, but says Clarity Act delays could prove advantageous
crypto-web3.summary: Mizuho Securities lowered its price target for digital asset custody company BitGo to $11 while maintaining a positive outlook based on the company's recurring revenue model and 27% year-over-year customer base growth. The analyst suggested that delays in cryptocurrency clarity legislation could ultimately benefit BitGo's competitive positioning.

energy-climate.title: Q&A: What does China's 15th five-year plan for coal mean for climate action?
energy-climate.summary: China has released a new five-year plan for coal that carries significant implications for global climate commitments. The policy document provides insight into China's coal strategy and its broader climate action framework during a critical period for emissions reduction.

energy-climate.title: Form Energy raises $750m to expand iron-air battery production
energy-climate.summary: Form Energy has secured $750 million in Series G financing led by T. Rowe Price to expand production of its iron-air battery technology. The funding underscores growing investor confidence in long-duration energy storage solutions critical for grid reliability and renewable energy integration.

energy-climate.title: The Hydrogen Stream: Commissioning begins for 2.2 GW Neom H2 project in Saudi Arabia
energy-climate.summary: Commissioning has commenced for a 2.2 GW hydrogen production facility at Saudi Arabia's Neom project, marking a major milestone in large-scale green hydrogen development. The project represents significant progress in hydrogen infrastructure, though a competing German hydrogen electrolyzer project was cancelled due to planning uncertainty.

energy-climate.title: Vikram Solar inaugurates 6 GW solar PV module factory in India
energy-climate.summary: Vikram Solar has commissioned a 6 GW solar PV module manufacturing facility in Tamil Nadu, bringing its total production capacity to 15.5 GW annually. The facility expansion reflects growing manufacturing capacity in India's renewable energy sector and supports increased solar deployment across Asia.

energy-climate.title: Noon Energy and Sabanci Renewables plan 1GW ultra-LDES project
energy-climate.summary: Noon Energy and Sabanci Renewables have announced a joint venture to develop up to 1 GW of ultra-long duration energy storage capacity. The partnership addresses the critical need for extended-duration storage solutions to support grid decarbonization and renewable energy reliability.

energy-climate.title: KIT develops hybrid solar system with radiative cooling
energy-climate.summary: Researchers at Karlsruhe Institute of Technology have developed an innovative hybrid system combining photovoltaics with passive radiative cooling to simultaneously generate electricity, heat, and cooling. The prototype demonstrated promising performance with 6.5°C below-ambient cooling and 60.6 W/m² electrical power density.

energy-climate.title: Chinese PV Industry Brief: Longi plans 100 MW perovskite-silicon tandem solar cell pilot line
energy-climate.summary: Longi is establishing a 100 MW pilot production line for perovskite-silicon tandem solar cells, with peers Trina Solar and Tongwei advancing complementary initiatives in next-generation photovoltaic technologies. These developments indicate accelerating commercialization of advanced solar cell architectures in China's competitive renewable energy sector.

energy-climate.title: Hillcore to build 2.6GW power complex at Fermi Matador site in US
energy-climate.summary: Fermi has signed a framework agreement with Hillcore to develop approximately 2.6 GW of generation capacity at its Project Matador campus in the United States. The development represents significant expansion of renewable and grid-supporting infrastructure in North America.

energy-climate.title: When heat becomes a stress test: What extreme temperatures mean for photovoltaic systems and battery storage
energy-climate.summary: Extreme heat presents operational challenges for solar photovoltaic systems and battery storage despite seeming advantageous for renewable generation and grid flexibility. The analysis explores performance degradation and reliability issues that emerge when temperature stress exceeds system design parameters.

energy-climate.title: Elemental Nuclear, Sandia Labs to partner on sCO₂ Brayton cycle project
energy-climate.summary: Elemental Nuclear has established a strategic partnership with Sandia National Laboratories to develop supercritical CO₂ Brayton Cycle Generator systems for advanced power generation. The collaboration advances development of high-efficiency thermal-to-electric conversion technology applicable to nuclear and renewable energy systems.

asia-pacific.title: China rattled by Trump White House chaos weeks ahead of Xi visit. It has happened before
asia-pacific.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping's planned state visit to Washington in less than six weeks is being complicated by organizational dysfunction within the Trump administration, mirroring frustrations from previous diplomatic preparations. Beijing's concerns over the chaotic preparation process underscore broader uncertainties in US-China relations at a critical diplomatic juncture.

asia-pacific.title: Taiwan Wants to Know Why Indonesia Joined China in a Naval Exercise East of Taiwan
asia-pacific.summary: Taiwan has raised concerns after Indonesia participated in Chinese naval exercises in waters east of Taiwan, an area of increasing strategic tension near Japan and the Philippines. The incident reflects growing regional military coordination involving China and represents a potential shift in regional alignments.

asia-pacific.title: Chinese drone maker DJI gets another shot at Pentagon blacklist removal
asia-pacific.summary: A US appeals court has granted Chinese drone manufacturer DJI another opportunity to challenge its inclusion on the Pentagon's defense blacklist, sending the case back to lower courts for reconsideration. The decision represents a potential shift in the years-long legal battle between the Shenzhen-based company and the US Department of Defence.

asia-pacific.title: China Forced Nepal to Cancel an International Conference on Tibetan Studies
asia-pacific.summary: China pressured Nepal to cancel an international conference on Tibetan studies, exemplifying Beijing's expanding efforts to assert control over Tibetan Buddhist affairs beyond its borders. The incident reveals China's increasingly assertive approach to managing narratives and institutions related to Tibet across the region.

asia-pacific.title: Restrictions on Foreign Fund Flow to Christian Organizations in India Complicate India-US Ties
asia-pacific.summary: India's proposed amendments to foreign funding regulations for Christian organizations are creating friction in India-US relations, with potential implications for broader trade negotiations. The dispute reflects deeper tensions between the two countries on issues of religious freedom and foreign policy alignment.

asia-pacific.title: Why India Needs a Comprehensive Polar Strategy
asia-pacific.summary: India remains conspicuously absent from major polar policy discussions despite the Arctic and Antarctic's growing importance to global climate and geopolitics. Strategic experts argue that India must develop comprehensive policies to engage in polar affairs where major powers are increasingly competing.

asia-pacific.title: Mecca Joint Deterrence Agreement: Implications for India
asia-pacific.summary: Pakistan is likely to leverage the Mecca Joint Deterrence Agreement among member states to strengthen its position during periods of tension with India. The pact's potential activation represents a significant factor in India's strategic calculations regarding regional security.

asia-pacific.title: URA posts HK$338 million operating surplus after three years of losses
asia-pacific.summary: Hong Kong's Urban Renewal Authority returned to profitability in the 2025-26 financial year with a HK$338 million operating surplus following three consecutive years of losses. The financial recovery enables the statutory body to fund ongoing urban renewal initiatives across the territory.

asia-pacific.title: In Afghanistan, Growing Resistance Meets Fears of Pakistani Influence
asia-pacific.summary: Afghan resistance movements are intensifying five years after the Taliban's return to power, while concerns mount over potential Pakistani involvement in anti-Taliban activities. The dynamic reflects continued regional instability and the complex geopolitical competition in Afghanistan.

asia-pacific.title: Singapore's Israel Tightrope
asia-pacific.summary: Singapore maintains a unique historical relationship with Israel among Asian nations, yet retains the diplomatic flexibility to pursue independent foreign policy positions. The city-state's balancing act reflects broader regional complexities in managing relationships between different stakeholders.
